newsitem.title: USA: Chad economy improved, more reforms needed - IMF.
newsitem.headline: Chad economy improved, more reforms needed - IMF.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund on Tuesday lauded Chad's overall economic performance since 1995 and the progress made on structural reforms, but noted some policy shortcomings in 1996.
In particular, Chad improved its external current account deficit and boosted non-agricultural economic activity, the IMF said in a report.
But overspending led to budgetary slippage in 1996, it said.

"The authorities needed to pursue adjustment efforts vigorously in order to strengthen fiscal discipline and to meet pressing public investment and social needs," the report said. "That would allow more room for private sector development and set the conditions for sustained economic growth."
The IMF urged Chad to improve economic statistics collection and accelerate civil service reforms, social security improvements and privatization, the report said.

For 1997, the IMF projected Chad's Gross Domestic Product would expand by 6.3 percent, compared with growth estimated at 2.7 percent last year. It forecast consumer prices would rise 7.1 percent on an annual basis this year, versus 11.3 percent in 1996.
IMF officials "observed that Chad's balance of payments outlook was expected to improve in the medium term," the report said.
